subtopics.title: The Four Core Regions and the Chosen Two

questions.question: South Africa's four core industrial regions are:
options: Gauteng (PWV), Durban–Pinetown, Port Elizabeth–Uitenhage, South-Western Cape

questions.question: The organising sentence for the map of the four regions is:
options: Minerals built Gauteng; harbours built the coastal three
Railways built the coast; roads built the interior

questions.question: The four rows of the case-study grid are:
options: Location factors; main activities; favouring and hindering factors; economic and social impacts

subtopics.title: Gauteng — the PWV: South Africa's Industrial Heart

questions.question: The letters PWV stand for:
Gauteng's missing water was engineered in through:
options: The Vaal Dam and the Lesotho Highlands scheme

questions.question: "Industrial regions outlive their reasons" fits Gauteng because:
options: Its coal was exhausted before its gold
The gold is nearly gone, yet the infrastructure, skills and market it gathered keep the region dominant

questions.question: Gauteng's chief locational handicap is that it has:
options: No port — every export pays the long overland leg to Durban

subtopics.title: Port Elizabeth–Uitenhage: The Motor Town on Algoa Bay

questions.question: The vehicle maker anchoring Kariega (formerly Uitenhage) is:
The component speciality linking this region to the platinum case study is:
The region's structural weakness is:
options: Too wide a spread of industries
Dependence on a single industry — the motor sector

questions.question: The modern deep-water port beside the region is:

subtopics.title: Spreading the Map: SDIs, Corridors, IDZs and SEZs

questions.question: The flagship Spatial Development Initiative runs:
options: From Gauteng through Mpumalanga to the harbour at Maputo

questions.question: The IDZ recipe is:
options: A serviced industrial estate at a port or airport with incentives, duty-free inputs for exporters and one-stop services

questions.question: Which zone-and-speciality pairing is correct?
options: Saldanha Bay — oil, gas and marine engineering

questions.question: The balanced verdict on SDIs and IDZs is that they:
options: Have evenly spread industry across all provinces
Steer some growth to new places but have not broken the four-region concentration

questions.question: In the train picture, over-concentration means:
options: All the pulling power coupled at four points, overheating them while the far coaches crawl and empty
Too many passengers on one train
Engines spread evenly along the line

questions.question: The South-Western Cape engine mainly hauls:
options: Food, wine, clothing and printing for its comfortable market

questions.question: The four pocket questions for any case study are:
options: Why there, what does it pull, what helps and hurts, who rides — who gains and who pays

subtopics.title: The Engine That Outlived Its Gold

questions.question: Gauteng drinks "through a very long straw" because:
options: It relies on desalinated sea water
Its water is pumped up from the Vaal Dam and Lesotho's mountains

questions.question: "The engine outlived the gold that built it" because Gauteng still holds:
options: The converging railways, the skills, Africa's richest market and thousands of linked firms
Most of the world's remaining gold

questions.question: "Gauteng is the workshop and the office at the same time" refers to:
options: Heavy industry plus Africa's densest banks and head offices

questions.question: The standard image of Gauteng's inequality is:
options: Sandton's towers facing Alexandra across a highway

subtopics.title: The Car Town, and Starting New Engines

questions.question: The car town's six-word location story is:
options: Gold, coal, water, rail, skills, market
Sun, soil, cane, mill, port, ship
Pass, bridge, border, gate, road, town
Port, rail, chosen by car makers

questions.question: "When the world pauses its car-buying, the whole town holds its breath" describes:
An IDZ as "a fully furnished flat for industry" means:
options: Ready-built infrastructure, services and incentives so export factories can move straight in
Free worker housing at every port

questions.question: The honest verdict on the new engines is:
options: Fully successful — industry is now evenly spread
A complete failure with no jobs created
Partly working — real factories at Coega and East London, but the four core regions still dominate
